recentItems.title: “GREET PUTIN WITH TOTAL SANCTIONS”: Ukraine calls on the world to counter to Russia’s terror
recentItems.description:
Russian occupiers struck a five-story apartment building in Pryluky, Chernihiv region, killing nine civilians, including three children, and injuring more than 30 people.

Residential areas of Kremenchuk also came under enemy attack. According to Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Ukraine’s energy infrastructure was once again the key target of the overnight assault.

At the same time, Ukraine’s Defence Forces held off more than 200 combat engagements along the front line and struck four strategic facilities deep inside Russia that helped finance the enemy’s war machine.

recentItems.title: 3,030 KM DEEP INSIDE Russia! Ukrainian drones ERASE THE NOTION OF “war far away”
recentItems.description:
Three thousand kilometres no longer guarantee Russia’s safety. This report covers drone attacks far from the Ukrainian border. Ukrainian unmanned systems are already reaching targets far beyond the Urals, while production of these systems continues to grow.

The consequences of strikes on oil refining, logistics, export terminals and companies linked to war financing extend far beyond the damaged facilities themselves. Russia is facing fuel shortages, falling oil revenues and export problems.

The map of the war now stretches across thousands of kilometres, and the notion of a “deep rear” is becoming increasingly relative for Russia.

recentItems.title: OIL DEPOT SERVING THREE AIRPORTS IS ON FIRE! Merz in Kyiv: 15 deals worth €8.5 BILLION & new F-16s!
recentItems.description:
A massive drone strike on an oil facility near Moscow that supplied aviation fuel to three Moscow airports caused a large-scale fire and paralysed the enemy’s aviation logistics.

Meanwhile, European allies are strengthening Ukraine’s F-16 fleet. The Netherlands is providing ammunition, spare parts and maintenance, while Belgium is preparing to transfer three additional fighter jets.

In addition, during his visit to Kyiv, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz signed 15 agreements with Ukraine worth a record €8.5 billion. The agreements are aimed at strengthening air defence and artillery, countering drones and preparing the energy system for winter.

recentItems.title: SENSATIONAL INTERVIEW WITH THE “FREEDOM OF RUSSIA” LEGION! Armed opposition cost Putin $10 million
recentItems.description:
In an interview, Maximilian “Caesar” Andronnikov, deputy commander of the Freedom of Russia Legion, said that Putin’s regime would be brought down not by émigré forums, but by armed front-line veterans and a relentless underground resistance.

The biggest revelation was the disclosure of details about Operation “Barrel”: partisans simultaneously targeted railway tank cars in 10 Russian regions, where the Kremlin had hidden fuel after attacks on oil refineries. More than 10,000 tonnes of oil worth at least $10 million were destroyed, blocking military transport by the occupiers’ trains.

“Caesar” also discussed the audacious operations carried out by his associates, including the arson attack on the Serpukhov missile corvette and the elimination of the battalion commander known as “The Butcher.” He explained why Russia’s covert mobilisation will inevitably end in a rebellion by frontline officers, following the scenario of 1917.

recentItems.title: TROJAN APC AND ROBOT DEPLOYMENT! Operation “Vivaldi” to continue into a FOURTH SEASON
recentItems.description:
Ukraine’s Defence Forces have moved to a new phase of Operation “Vivaldi” in Donbas: an airborne deployment of assault robots behind enemy lines and a raid using the “Trojan APC” tactic sowed panic among the occupiers and breached their defences, destroying entire columns of military equipment.

In response to colossal losses, the Kremlin is launching another mobilisation wave of 300,000 people. However, these plans are being undermined by a Ukrainian armada of hundreds of long-range attack drones, which are systematically burning down military bases, ammunition depots and logistics hubs deep inside Russia.
